description: A heavy fixed press, screwed down by hand, in which piles of sections or finished books are left under sustained pressure to set them solid. The iron form is tightened with a short then a long bar; the French form drives the screw with a weighted spinning wheel that also hammers the work tight.
name: standing press

source_ref.label: Douglas Cockerell, Bookbinding and the Care of Books (1902), Chapter V, p.89. Internet Archive.
